_comment: Servo counts for a level (horizontal) lidar scan plane. Captured with the mount physically level; re-run src/lidar_tilt.py --calibrate after any remount.
_tilt_direction_comment: +1 = increasing counts pitches the lidar nose-DOWN (the URDF's positive lidar_tilt_joint). VERIFIED 2026-08-23, see direction_verification.

servo_state_at_calibration._pos_counts_note: was 12 (=2.88 deg) until 2026-08-23: a single corrupt read_pos on the half-duplex bus, written by read_state() seconds after calibrate() sampled 500 fifteen times with zero spread. Re-measured live at 500 with 300/300 clean reads (only 499-500 seen). Repaired to 500.

note: first calibration after the new tilting mount was installed

direction_verification.method: Raw /scan_raw only, no URDF and no TF. The floor is 0.340 m below the lidar and the ceiling ~2.1 m above, so a 30 deg tilt puts the downhill side on the floor at slant range 0.34/sin30 = 0.68 m while the uphill side reaches ~4.2 m. The SHORT return therefore marks the downhill bearing. Comparing +30 against -30 does NOT work: a global sign flip only swaps which physical station is labelled +30, so both look sensible either way (that first attempt returned 0.0% anomalies at every station).
direction_verification.reasoning: At raised counts the floor sits at laser bearing 180, so laser_link's +X pitched UP. laser_joint yaws laser_link 180 deg from lidar_tilt_link, so lidar_tilt_link's +X pitched DOWN, which for a rotation about +Y is a POSITIVE joint angle => direction = +1. The driver's inverted:=true flips the sign of the bearing and so cannot affect a 0-versus-180 test.
direction_verification.physical_confirmation: Operator watched both runs: at raised counts the front of the mount (the OAK-D end) dipped down toward the floor ahead of the robot.
direction_verification.level_cross_check: Floor slant range was 0.65 m raised vs 0.64 m lowered -- symmetric about 500 counts. At 30 deg, d(range)/d(tilt) = 0.021 m/deg, so that 1 cm difference confirms horizontal_counts=500 is level to ~0.25 deg.
direction_verification._height_note: 0.340 m above base_footprint, measured via TF: a level scan projected to a perfectly flat plane at z=+0.340 across 81872 points. The 0.191 m quoted in several code comments is the OLD pre-tilting-mount height and is stale.
